title: Three Seasons and One Short Whistle
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：sweat　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sweat 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the coach ① wiped the sweat that no player in the field would have counted, and he said the wiping was the whole of the season. The ② sweat, meaning the moisture itself and not the whistle, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; sweat, he said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ sort of sweat in that field had the same short whistle beside it, and the ④ sweat at the far stand, meaning the goal they kept for the children to cheer and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Sweat, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the coach said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sweat was the whole of the matter, meaning the effort and not the moisture. The ⑥ sweat, meaning the effort and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; sweat, he said, is either something you wipe or the only word that means both moisture and an effort. He said the effort is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ sweat had become a line in a record, and the record had become an argument about the short whistle. The ⑧ sweat of the whole thing, the coach wrote in April, was one field and three seasons of counting; sweat, he said, is either the goal at the far stand or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sweat I remember is the sweat counted in the record, which closed in 1963 and is still counted as the quietest in the field. ⑩ Sweat, my mother said in 1965, is the only thing that improves by being counted; all sweat, she said, is an effort that has agreed to look like moisture. She said the effort was the honest half.

task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。

B. n. 汗（指那滴汗本身，与小小的哨子相对）
C. 固定搭配：wipe the sweat 擦这一滴汗

answers.why: wipe the sweat 意为“擦这一滴汗”，1956 年那位教练把球场里没有一位队员肯清点的一滴汗做了一遍。
sweat 意为“汗”，指那滴汗本身而不是小小的哨子，它经过了三个赛季而在簿子上没有被清点。
sweat 意为“汗”，指球场里每一类旁边的那一类，每一类旁边都有同一只小小的哨子。
sweat 意为“汗”，指最远那面看台的留给孩子们喊的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sweat 意为“汗、辛苦”，指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这滴辛苦就是那件事的全部。
sweat 意为“辛苦”，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西而不是那滴汗，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sweat 意为“汗”，指赛事记录里写到、被清点的那一滴，到 1961 年这一滴成了赛事记录里的一行。
sweat 意为“汗之事”，教练四月写道，整件事的汗之事是一处球场和三个赛季的清点。
sweat 意为“汗”，我记得的是赛事记录里清点过的那一滴，1963 年打完了，至今仍被说成球场里最安静的一滴。
sweat 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，汗是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的汗。
